main_text.l: frigidioribus, nempe apoplexiam, paraly-
sim, epilepsia, catalepsim, & alia id genus.
Haec breviter de commodis & incommo-
dis Lunae, e quibus humores nostri corpo-
ris, nec alius cuiusvis sanguinei animalis
per singula plenilunia non crescere: nec p
interlunia ipsos quoq; decrescere, collige-
re possumus. Adde quod si plenilunio ple-
thora & humorum plenitas esset tribuen-
da, certe nulla opus foret evacuatione, sed
relinquenda esset sequenti, & proximo in-
terlunio: quando videlicet necessario fie-
ret vasorum inanitio. Proinde vana esset
nostri boni senis Hippocrat. doctrina, qua
passim, & præsertim[?] suis in aphorismis ple-
thora evacuatione per sanguinis emissio-
nem, ut & cacochymiam purgatione esse
soluendam docemur. Nec præterea au-
diendi sunt, qui acutorum morborum cri-
ses ipsius Lunae ui & motui attribuunt.
Nam si id esset, profecto exquisitae (exem-
pli causa) omnes tertianae, quæ eodem tem-
pore quoslibet invadunt, eodem æque mo-
mento indicarentur. Sed alias alijs celeri-
us (licet eadem hora simul inceperint, ua-
riosque invaserint) & alias tardius iudicari,
finiriq; norut[?] satis omnes medici. Propte-
Cf. the printed text above for the catchword "rea", which begins the following page.

page.notes: Page number "65" is printed at the top right; the final digit is partly unclear, hence [?]. "vasorum" is read from a damaged word and is uncertain; the printed letters look like "uasorum". "præsertim" and "norut" are doubtful readings. The line ending "Propte-" continues on the next page, with "rea" as the catchword. The printed "ple-thora" and "paraly-sim" are line-end hyphenations kept as printed.
